types.embedding_query_text: Organization: A structured group of people with a particular purpose, such as a business, government department, or sports governing body. Also called Association, Body, Institution, Federation. Examples: UEFA, FIFA, CONMEBOL, European soccer's governing body.

chosen_type.label: Organization
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type 'Organization' and its definition directly match schema.org's Organization, which is a general group of people with a purpose, fitting the mentions.

candidates.label: Organization
candidates.comment: An Organization is a group of people with a particular purpose, such as a school, NGO, corporation, or club. Also called entity, institution, association. Examples: Google, Harvard University, Red Cross, a local sports club. Distinct from Person, which is an individual.

candidates.label: SportsOrganization
candidates.comment: A general category for organizations involved in sports, including teams, governing bodies, and associations. Also called athletic organization, sports body, sports group. Examples: the NBA, a local youth soccer league, the International Olympic Committee.

candidates.label: SportsTeam
candidates.comment: An organization consisting of a group of athletes who compete together in a sport. Also called athletic team, squad, club, side. Examples: the Los Angeles Lakers, the New England Patriots, a high school basketball team.

candidates.label: MedicalOrganization
candidates.comment: An organization, physical or virtual, operating in the medical domain, such as a hospital or clinic. Also called healthcare organization, medical institution, health system. Examples: "Mayo Clinic", "World Health Organization", "Doctors Without Borders". Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category for any group.

candidates.label: GovernmentOrganization
candidates.comment: A GovernmentOrganization is an organization or agency that is part of a governmental body. Also called public sector entity, state agency, governmental body. Examples: Department of Defense, Environmental Protection Agency, National Institutes of Health, local city council.

types.embedding_query_text: Competition: An event or contest in which people or teams compete against each other. Also called Tournament, Championship, Match, Event. Examples: FIFA competitions, World Cup, major competitions.

chosen_type.label: SportsEvent
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type 'Competition' and the mention 'FIFA competitions' are perfectly described by schema.org's SportsEvent, which covers athletic competitions.

candidates.label: SportsEvent
candidates.comment: An event involving athletic competition or display. Also called athletic contest, game, match, sporting competition. Examples: a football game, an Olympic event, a marathon race, a tennis tournament.

candidates.label: Event
candidates.comment: An Event is a Thing happening at a specific time and location, such as a concert, lecture, or festival. Also called happening, occurrence, occasion. Examples: A rock concert, a public lecture, a sports match, a community festival.

candidates.label: SportsTeam
candidates.comment: An organization consisting of a group of athletes who compete together in a sport. Also called athletic team, squad, club, side. Examples: the Los Angeles Lakers, the New England Patriots, a high school basketball team.

candidates.label: ConferenceEvent
candidates.comment: An event specifically organized as a conference, typically involving presentations, discussions, and networking. Also called conference, convention, symposium, summit. Examples: A tech conference, an academic symposium, a business summit, a medical convention. Distinct from Event, which is a general occurrence.

candidates.label: SportsOrganization
candidates.comment: A general category for organizations involved in sports, including teams, governing bodies, and associations. Also called athletic organization, sports body, sports group. Examples: the NBA, a local youth soccer league, the International Olympic Committee.

types.embedding_query_text: Situation: A set of circumstances in which one finds oneself; a state of affairs. Also called Circumstance, Condition, State, Scenario. Examples: FIFA crisis, turbulence.

chosen_type.label: CrisisSituation
chosen_type.definition: A serious or difficult state of affairs requiring immediate attention.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class adequately captures 'Situation' or 'crisis' as an ongoing state of affairs; existing event types are too specific to discrete happenings.

candidates.label: Event
candidates.comment: An Event is a Thing happening at a specific time and location, such as a concert, lecture, or festival. Also called happening, occurrence, occasion. Examples: A rock concert, a public lecture, a sports match, a community festival.

candidates.label: SportsEvent
candidates.comment: An event involving athletic competition or display. Also called athletic contest, game, match, sporting competition. Examples: a football game, an Olympic event, a marathon race, a tennis tournament.

candidates.label: Error
candidates.comment: An Error is an InstantaneousEvent representing a problem or failure that occurred. Also called fault, malfunction, issue. Examples: A 404 Not Found error, a database connection error, a system crash, a data validation error.

candidates.label: EventStatusType
candidates.comment: An EventStatusType is a StatusEnumeration whose instances represent various states an Event may be in. Also called event state, status of event. Examples: EventScheduled, EventCancelled, EventPostponed, EventRescheduled.

candidates.label: WantAction
candidates.comment: The act of expressing a desire or wish for an object or outcome. Also called desire, wish for, covet. Examples: wanting a new car, desiring a specific job, wishing for peace.

types.embedding_query_text: Person: An individual human being. Also called Individual, Human, Leader, Official. Examples: Gianni Infantino, FIFA president, president.

chosen_type.label: Person
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type 'Person' and the mention 'Gianni Infantino' are a direct and exact match for schema.org's Person.

candidates.label: Person
candidates.comment: A Person is an individual human being, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional. Also called individual, human, character. Examples: John Doe, Albert Einstein, Sherlock Holmes. Distinct from Organization, which is a group of people.

candidates.label: Organization
candidates.comment: An Organization is a group of people with a particular purpose, such as a school, NGO, corporation, or club. Also called entity, institution, association. Examples: Google, Harvard University, Red Cross, a local sports club. Distinct from Person, which is an individual.

candidates.label: SportsOrganization
candidates.comment: A general category for organizations involved in sports, including teams, governing bodies, and associations. Also called athletic organization, sports body, sports group. Examples: the NBA, a local youth soccer league, the International Olympic Committee.

candidates.label: Country
candidates.comment: A Country is a sovereign state or nation, representing a primary administrative division of the Earth's surface. Also called nation, state, sovereign state, realm. Examples: United States, Canada, France, Japan, Brazil.

candidates.label: SportsTeam
candidates.comment: An organization consisting of a group of athletes who compete together in a sport. Also called athletic team, squad, club, side. Examples: the Los Angeles Lakers, the New England Patriots, a high school basketball team.

types.embedding_query_text: Country: A nation with its own government, occupying a particular territory. Also called Nation, State, Land, Realm. Examples: Morocco.

chosen_type.label: Country
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type 'Country' and the mention 'Morocco' are a direct and exact match for schema.org's Country.

candidates.label: Country
candidates.comment: A Country is a sovereign state or nation, representing a primary administrative division of the Earth's surface. Also called nation, state, sovereign state, realm. Examples: United States, Canada, France, Japan, Brazil.

candidates.label: State
candidates.comment: A major administrative division of a country, such as a state or province. Also called province, region, territory, commonwealth. Examples: California, Ontario, Bavaria, Texas.

candidates.label: AdministrativeArea
candidates.comment: An AdministrativeArea is a geographical region, typically governed by a specific authority. Also called political division, jurisdiction, governmental region, territory. Examples: A country, a state, a province, a city, a county.

candidates.label: Continent
candidates.comment: One of the Earth's large landmasses, such as Europe or Africa. Also called major landmass, global region, land continent. Examples: Asia, North America, Antarctica, Australia. Distinct from Landform, which is a general term for a natural feature of the Earth's surface.

candidates.label: Mountain
candidates.comment: A landform that is a large natural elevation of the earth's surface, typically rising to a summit. Also called peak, mount, range. Examples: "Mount Everest", "Mount Fuji", "Rocky Mountains", "Mount Kilimanjaro". Distinct from Landform, which is a broader category for natural geographical features.

types.embedding_query_text: Date: A particular day, month, or year, often specified in the text. Also called Day, Time, Period, Moment. Examples: Wednesday, Saturday, Thursday, yesterday.

chosen_type.label: DayOfWeek
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type 'Date' with mentions like 'Wednesday' specifically refers to days of the week, which is precisely what schema.org's DayOfWeek represents.

candidates.label: Date
candidates.comment: Date is a data type representing a specific calendar date, typically formatted according to ISO 8601. Also called calendar date, specific day. Examples: "2023-10-27", "1999-12-31", "0001-01-01".

candidates.label: DayOfWeek
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing a specific day of the week, used for scheduling or recurring events. Also called Weekday, calendar day, day name. Examples: Monday, Tuesday, Saturday, Sunday. Distinct from Date, which specifies a particular calendar date.

candidates.label: DateTime
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, combining both date and time components according to ISO 8601. Also called Timestamp, date and time string, ISO 8601 datetime. Examples: "2023-10-27T10:30:00Z", "1999-12-31T23:59:59-05:00", "2024-01-15T14:00:00". Distinct from Date, which only specifies a calendar date without time.

candidates.label: Time
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, typically in hh:mm:ss format, potentially with a timezone offset. Also called timestamp, clock time, time of day. Examples: "14:30:00", "09:00:00Z", "17:45:30+01:00".

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

types.embedding_query_text: Plan: A detailed proposal for doing or achieving something. Also called Scheme, Project, Proposal, Strategy. Examples: FIFA's Private Investor Plan, failed plan to sell stakes in the World Cup, proposals to sell off the major competitions, controversial plan to sell profits in the World Cup through a commercial subsidiary.

chosen_type.label: ProposalPlan
chosen_type.definition: A detailed scheme or program for achieving an objective.
chosen_type.justification: Existing schema.org candidates are either organizations (Project) or actions (PlanAction), not the conceptual 'plan' itself as described by the OIE type and mention.

candidates.label: Project
candidates.comment: A Project is an Organization representing an enterprise, typically collaborative, planned to achieve a particular aim. Also called initiative, endeavor, venture. Examples: a software development project, a construction project, a research initiative, a community outreach program.

candidates.label: ResearchProject
candidates.comment: A ResearchProject is a Project representing a planned enterprise aimed at scientific or academic inquiry. Also called research initiative, study, academic project. Examples: a clinical trial, a grant-funded scientific study, a historical research project, a university-led exploration.

candidates.label: PlanAction
candidates.comment: PlanAction is an OrganizeAction that involves arranging the execution of an event, task, action, reservation, or plan for a future time. Also called scheduling, arranging, pre-arranging. Examples: planning a wedding, scheduling a meeting, arranging a trip itinerary, setting up a project timeline.

candidates.label: ExercisePlan
candidates.comment: An ExercisePlan is a CreativeWork representing a fitness-related activity designed for a specific health purpose, including routines or clinician-prescribed activities. Also called workout plan, fitness regimen, training program. Examples: A 30-day weight loss plan, a physical therapy exercise routine, a marathon training schedule, a yoga sequence.

candidates.label: ScheduleAction
candidates.comment: The act of planning and allocating future actions, events, or tasks to specific time slots or spatial allocations. Also called planning, arranging, organizing, booking. Examples: scheduling a doctor's appointment, booking a meeting room, planning a project timeline, arranging a delivery. Distinct from ReserveAction, which implies making a reservation for a specific resource or service.

types.embedding_query_text: Condition: A state that must exist or be met for something else to happen. Also called Prerequisite, Requirement, Stipulation, Term. Examples: Withdrawal of Sales Proposals, Assurances Against Future Attempts.

chosen_type.label: RequirementCondition
chosen_type.definition: A state or prerequisite that must be met for something else to occur.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class captures the general concept of a 'Condition' as a prerequisite; existing candidates are too specific (e.g., medical, item, incentive status) or are actions.

candidates.label: IncentiveStatus
candidates.comment: IncentiveStatus is an enumeration describing the current status of an incentive, such as whether it is active or expired. Also called incentive state, benefit status, program condition. Examples: 'Active', 'Expired', 'Pending', 'Suspended'.

candidates.label: OfferItemCondition
candidates.comment: OfferItemCondition is an enumeration listing possible conditions for an item being offered. Also called item state, product condition, quality status. Examples: NewCondition, UsedCondition, RefurbishedCondition, DamagedCondition. Distinct from OfferShippingDetails, which describes shipping logistics.

candidates.label: MedicalCondition
candidates.comment: A medical entity representing any condition of the human body that affects normal functioning, including diseases, injuries, disabilities, and disorders. Also called disease, illness, health disorder, ailment. Examples: "influenza", "diabetes", "a broken arm", "depression", "asthma".

candidates.label: PreOrderAction
candidates.comment: PreOrderAction is a TradeAction where an agent orders an object, product, or service that is not yet released, for future delivery. Also called pre-booking, advance ordering. Examples: pre-ordering a new video game, reserving an upcoming book, pre-booking a new car model, ordering a limited edition item before release.

candidates.label: WantAction
candidates.comment: The act of expressing a desire or wish for an object or outcome. Also called desire, wish for, covet. Examples: wanting a new car, desiring a specific job, wishing for peace.

types.embedding_query_text: GroupOfPeople: A collection of individuals forming a unit or working together. Also called Team, Staff, Personnel, Collective. Examples: Top Staff, some people employed by the FIFA president.

chosen_type.label: StaffGroup
chosen_type.definition: A collection of individuals working together within an organization.
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type 'GroupOfPeople' and mention 'Top Staff' refer to a specific group within an organization, which is not directly covered by schema.org's general Organization or specific performing groups.

candidates.label: SportsTeam
candidates.comment: An organization consisting of a group of athletes who compete together in a sport. Also called athletic team, squad, club, side. Examples: the Los Angeles Lakers, the New England Patriots, a high school basketball team.

candidates.label: SportsOrganization
candidates.comment: A general category for organizations involved in sports, including teams, governing bodies, and associations. Also called athletic organization, sports body, sports group. Examples: the NBA, a local youth soccer league, the International Olympic Committee.

candidates.label: Organization
candidates.comment: An Organization is a group of people with a particular purpose, such as a school, NGO, corporation, or club. Also called entity, institution, association. Examples: Google, Harvard University, Red Cross, a local sports club. Distinct from Person, which is an individual.

candidates.label: PerformingGroup
candidates.comment: A PerformingGroup is an organization of performers, such as a band, orchestra, or circus. Also called performance ensemble, troupe, artistic group. Examples: Cirque du Soleil, a local theatre company, a dance troupe. Distinct from MusicGroup, which is specifically for musical performers.

candidates.label: MusicGroup
candidates.comment: A MusicGroup, as a PerformingGroup, is an organization of musicians, such as a band or orchestra, or a solo musician. Also called band, musical ensemble, orchestra, solo artist. Examples: The Beatles, New York Philharmonic, Taylor Swift. Distinct from PerformingGroup, which is a broader category for any performance group.

types.embedding_query_text: Reaction: A response to a particular event, situation, or idea. Also called Response, Feedback, Repercussion, Outcome. Examples: Widespread Condemnation.

chosen_type.label: ReactAction
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type 'Reaction' and mention 'Widespread Condemnation' align well with schema.org's ReactAction, which represents expressing sentiment or a response.

candidates.label: ReactAction
candidates.comment: ReactAction is an AssessAction representing the act of responding instinctively and emotionally to an object, expressing a sentiment. Also called emotional response, sentiment expression. Examples: liking a social media post, disliking a video, expressing shock at news, showing approval for an idea.

candidates.label: DislikeAction
candidates.comment: A react action expressing a negative sentiment or disapproval towards an object, proposition, or theme. Also called Express dislike, disapprove of, show aversion, downvote. Examples: Disliking a movie, expressing disapproval of a policy, downvoting a comment online. Distinct from LikeAction, which expresses positive sentiment or approval.

candidates.label: DisagreeAction
candidates.comment: A react action expressing a negative opinion or difference of opinion regarding an object, proposition, or theme. Also called Express disagreement, object to, dispute, dissent. Examples: Disagreeing with a political statement, objecting to a proposed plan, disputing a fact. Distinct from AgreeAction, which expresses positive sentiment or agreement.

candidates.label: AssessAction
candidates.comment: An AssessAction is an Action involving the formation of an opinion, reaction, or sentiment about something. Also called evaluate, appraise, judge, review, rate. Examples: a critic reviewing a movie, a teacher grading an assignment, a user rating a product, a doctor evaluating a patient's condition.

candidates.label: WantAction
candidates.comment: The act of expressing a desire or wish for an object or outcome. Also called desire, wish for, covet. Examples: wanting a new car, desiring a specific job, wishing for peace.

types.embedding_query_text: LeadershipRole: The position or function of a leader within an organization or group. Also called Management, Headship, Directorship, Command. Examples: FIFA's leadership.

chosen_type.label: OrganizationRole
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type 'LeadershipRole' and mention 'FIFA's leadership' refer to a function or position within an organization, which is precisely what schema.org's OrganizationRole describes.

candidates.label: OrganizationRole
candidates.comment: An OrganizationRole, as a Role, describes a specific function or position within an organization. Also called organizational position, corporate role, job title. Examples: CEO, Marketing Manager, Board Member, Volunteer Coordinator. Distinct from Role, which is a broader category for any role.

candidates.label: EmployeeRole
candidates.comment: An EmployeeRole is an OrganizationRole describing the relationship of an individual as an employee within an organization. Also called job position, staff role, employment status. Examples: "Software Engineer" at Google, "Marketing Manager" at a startup, "Cashier" at a supermarket.

candidates.label: PerformanceRole
candidates.comment: A PerformanceRole, as a Role, is a role an entity plays in a theatrical performance, such as a movie or TV series. Also called acting role, character role, stage role. Examples: 'actor in a film', 'director of a play', 'musician in a concert'. Distinct from OrganizationRole, which is a role within an organization.

candidates.label: SportsTeam
candidates.comment: An organization consisting of a group of athletes who compete together in a sport. Also called athletic team, squad, club, side. Examples: the Los Angeles Lakers, the New England Patriots, a high school basketball team.

candidates.label: SportsOrganization
candidates.comment: A general category for organizations involved in sports, including teams, governing bodies, and associations. Also called athletic organization, sports body, sports group. Examples: the NBA, a local youth soccer league, the International Olympic Committee.

types.embedding_query_text: PotentialEvent: An event that is possible or likely to happen in the future. Also called Prospective event, Future occurrence, Likely event, Impending event. Examples: Challenge to Presidency.

chosen_type.label: ProspectiveEvent
chosen_type.definition: An event that is anticipated or likely to occur in the future.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class directly represents a 'PotentialEvent' or an event that is likely to happen; existing event types describe actual occurrences.

candidates.label: DeliveryEvent
candidates.comment: An event representing the delivery of an item, typically a product or package. Also called Shipping event, package delivery, consignment event. Examples: A package arriving at its destination, a food delivery being completed, a furniture delivery appointment. Distinct from Order, which is the request for items, not the delivery itself.

candidates.label: SportsEvent
candidates.comment: An event involving athletic competition or display. Also called athletic contest, game, match, sporting competition. Examples: a football game, an Olympic event, a marathon race, a tennis tournament.

candidates.label: ConferenceEvent
candidates.comment: An event specifically organized as a conference, typically involving presentations, discussions, and networking. Also called conference, convention, symposium, summit. Examples: A tech conference, an academic symposium, a business summit, a medical convention. Distinct from Event, which is a general occurrence.

candidates.label: LiteraryEvent
candidates.comment: An event focused on literature, such as readings, book launches, or discussions. Also called book event, author appearance, literary gathering. Examples: a poetry reading, a book signing, a literary festival, a panel discussion with authors.

candidates.label: TheaterEvent
candidates.comment: An event representing a live performance in a theater. Also called stage play, theatrical show, drama performance. Examples: a Broadway musical, a local community play, a Shakespearean tragedy.

types.embedding_query_text: ActionPattern: A recurring or characteristic sequence of actions or behaviors. Also called Behavioral pattern, Course of action, Trend, Habit. Examples: Repeated Unilateral Actions.

chosen_type.label: ActionSequence
chosen_type.definition: A recurring or characteristic series of actions or behaviors.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class captures the concept of an 'ActionPattern' or 'Repeated Unilateral Actions' as a sequence or characteristic behavior; existing candidates are single actions.

candidates.label: MoveAction
candidates.comment: An action where a living agent, such as a person or organization, relocates to a different place. Also called relocate, transfer residence, change location. Examples: moving to a new city, a company relocating its headquarters, a person walking to another room. Distinct from TransferAction, where the subject being moved is an inanimate object.

candidates.label: SeekToAction
candidates.comment: The action of navigating to a specific timestamp within a video object, typically using a URL parameter. Also called jump to time, fast forward to, skip to, go to timestamp. Examples: clicking a link that starts a YouTube video at 2:30, using a video player's seek bar.

candidates.label: DepartAction
candidates.comment: A move action representing the act of an agent leaving a specific location to travel towards a destination. Also called Leave, set off, embark, exit. Examples: A plane departing from an airport, a person leaving their home for work, a ship sailing from a port. Distinct from ArriveAction, which is the act of reaching a destination.

candidates.label: WatchAction
candidates.comment: The act of consuming dynamic or moving visual content. Also called view, observe, see. Examples: watching a movie, watching a live sports broadcast, watching a video tutorial.

candidates.label: UpdateAction
candidates.comment: The act of managing or changing the state or content of an object. Also called modify, edit, revise. Examples: updating a software application, editing a document, changing a profile picture.
